title: Rung manifest
description: The single authority on what a rung is. See rungs.json's _readme.

shapes.description: Closed set of interaction shapes. #23 ruled that shape is a declared rung property and the shell routes by it. Adding a shape is a deliberate edit here plus a new branch in the shell's handler.

states.description: Vocabulary for `state`, with the meaning of each spelled out so it cannot drift.

requires.description: The superset chain: rung N requires N-1. eject retains the transitive closure downward, never a bare single rung.

languages.description: Which language planes contain files owned by this rung, and therefore must be INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED after an eject. Not 'which languages implement the agent'. This drives the CI matrix arity: 3 bilingual rungs + 2 ts-only = 8 jobs. A 5-job matrix would run pnpm-only tooling and show green over a Python plane that eject edited and nothing executed.

target.description: WHERE THE SHELL SENDS YOU. Distinct from `owns`, which is which files die on eject. A rung's files and its entry point are different things: rungs 1-3 own files in two language planes but share one surface; rung 4 owns a whole app on another origin. There is deliberately NO `route` variant for a rung with its own in-app route: none exists, and a variant no rung exercises cannot be tested, rots, and reads to a reviewer as 'handled'. Adding one later is a schema line plus a compile error from assertNever() pointing at the exact switch that needs a branch.

oneOf.title: param — a rung selected by a parameter on a shared surface

route.description: Route template containing the literal [<param>]. SUBSTITUTION RULE: the shell replaces [<param>] in this string with `value`. Stated here so it is a contract, not a convention anyone has to infer — rungHref() in rungs.generated.ts is the single implementation.

oneOf.title: origin — a rung served from a different origin
none — declared but not present; the shell must render it without offering a link

owns.description: WHICH FILES DIE when a lower rung is ejected. Globs are matched against git-tracked files only, so node_modules and build output never enter the census.

docs.description: Documentation owned by this rung. Separate from ts/py because C5 asks whether a PLANNED rung has shipped SOURCE — the ladder documents rungs before they exist, so counting docs would make that tripwire fire on docs/rungs/5-*.md and then get 'fixed' by weakening it.

ownedFileCount.description: Checked-in census, frozen by scripts/classify.ts. CHECK-2 asserts |deleted| EQUALS the sum of these for dropped rungs — an exact equality, so it cannot pass on a no-op (0 != 97) or on over-deletion (112 != 97). A `planned` rung MUST be 0; the tripwire fails CI if a file starts claiming one.

runtimes.description: Which backends SERVE this rung, and the topologies each one offers. PER (RUNG, RUNTIME), never per rung: the ladder has exactly one ragged cell -- deep-research exists only in deepagents x fastapi. A rung-level topologies[] cannot express that and would either emit a django x deep-research cell that 404s or drop fastapi's real one. NOT the same as `languages`: languages = which planes hold files this rung OWNS (drives the eject matrix); runtimes = which backends SERVE it (drives the behavioural matrix).

topologies.description: Topologies this (rung, runtime) pair serves. AN EMPTY ARRAY MEANS ONE CELL WITH NO TOPOLOGY AXIS -- NOT ZERO CELLS. `run` rungs have no topology axis; if empty collapsed to zero they would vanish from the matrix silently. Do not re-derive this rule per consumer: rungs.generated.ts exports matrixCells(), which encodes it once.

topologiesSource.description: The module whose TOPOLOGIES mapping defines this list. REQUIRED whenever topologies is non-empty: C8 parses it and fails if the two disagree, so the manifest cannot drift from the backend. An empty topologies list needs no source -- that is an absence of a claim, not an unverified one.

shared.description: Rung-agnostic paths. An ENUMERATED ALLOWLIST, never a fallback — a rung file must not become shared by being forgotten. Evaluated after rung ownership; rung ownership always wins.

_censusNote.description: Why only two shared globs have frozen membership (scripts/shared-census.json), with the measured churn and the condition for revisiting. Prose, so free-form lines -- but declared here because `shared` is additionalProperties:false, and a manifest key nobody declared is exactly what that setting exists to reject.

_rendererNote.description: Why each rung-named renderer in packages/react is or is not rung-owned. Prose, because the reasoning is per-file and the rule alone does not reproduce it.

not.description: Fields deliberately excluded. Stream topology does NOT belong in the manifest: real Open SWE registers three graphs that do not share a run, so a per-rung threadId, runId, or single stream endpoint would bake in a topology already known to be wrong (apps/open-swe/docs/LOCAL-AGENT.md, 'Topology: this backend is single-run'). Declaring `shape` is enough; the shape handler owns everything downstream.
